newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Indian Ocean airlines to set up regional airline.
newsitem.headline: Indian Ocean airlines to set up regional airline.

text.p: National airlines from Mauritius, Madagascar and the Seychelles have signed an agreement with Air France to create an Indian Ocean regional carrier, Air Mauritius said on Friday.
Air Mauritius chairman and managing director Nashir Mallam-Hasham said the southwest Indian Ocean airline would promote long haul and multi-destination traffic.
"The target set by the founder airlines is to start operations with the new regional airline as from mid 1998," he said.
Air Mauritius, Air Seychelles, Air Madagascar and Air France, which signed the agreement in a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday, also aim to improve air links with southern and eastern Africa.

"The shareholding of the regional airline company would be extended to private sectors of the countries of the region. Priority would be given to those private operators who work closely with the air transport sector," said Mallam-Hasham.
Asked if the new project was a strategy to kill the private sector African Islands Airways project, Mallam-Hasham said the two were totally different.
"Our new airline is a consortium that involves the airlines of the region," he said.
